questions.q: Name two physical properties that generally distinguish metals from non-metals.
questions.a: Metals are typically lustrous (shiny) and good conductors of electricity, while non-metals are typically dull and poor conductors. A wrong answer here suggests the student is confusing physical properties with chemical ones or simply guessing without reading the definitions.

questions.q: If you find a material that is dull and breaks easily when you hit it with a hammer, is it likely a metal or a non-metal?
questions.a: It is likely a non-metal. If a student says "metal," they have failed to connect the property of "hardness" and "lustre" to the definition of metals, indicating a need to re-examine the physical characteristics provided in the text.

questions.q: A piece of copper wire conducts electricity, but a piece of plastic tube does not. How does this help us categorize them?
questions.a: Copper is a metal because it conducts electricity, and plastic is a non-metal because it is a poor conductor. The student must use the property of conductivity as a test; a wrong answer shows they are not applying the "conductor" criteria to the classification process.

questions.q: Why do we say that "all that glitters is not gold" when classifying metals?
questions.a: Some non-metals or synthetic materials can be made to look shiny through polishing or coatings, even though they aren't metals. A wrong answer indicates the student is over-relying on the single property of "shine" without considering other properties like hardness or conductivity.

questions.q: If an object is very hard but does not conduct heat, would you classify it as a metal? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, it is likely not a metal because metals generally possess both hardness and the ability to conduct heat. A wrong answer shows the student thinks one property (hardness) is enough for classification, ignoring the requirement for multiple properties.

questions.q: Design a simple test to determine if a mysterious, unlabelled rod found in your garage is a metal.
questions.a: The student should suggest: 1) Checking if it is shiny (lustre), 2) Checking if it is hard (cannot be scratched by a fingernail), and 3) Testing if it conducts electricity (using a battery and bulb). A poor answer fails to list at least two distinct properties, showing a lack of systematic observation skills.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Metals are elements typically ______ by a shiny (lustrous) appearance, hardness, and the ability to conduct heat and electricity, whereas non-metals generally lack these properties, appearing dull and acting as poor conductors.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever wondered why your kitchen spoons are made of stainless steel while your water bottle might be made of ______?
What is Metals? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Metals are elements typically characterized by a shiny (lustrous) appearance, hardness, and the ability to conduct heat and electricity, whereas non-metals generally lack these properties, appearing dull and acting as poor conductors.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Metals?
questions.a: Students often believe that because a material is shiny, it MUST be a metal.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to classify a given list of common materials into metals and non-metals based on experimental observations like shine, hardness, and conductivity.
